items.title: Adobe Max 2026 Live Updates: All the AI, Photo and Video News - CNET
items.summary: The biggest changes are the general release of AI assistants in Photoshop, Adobe Express and its AI hub, Firefly, first teased at last year’s conference. These assistants are similar to chatbots, where you enter your request and the AI does the editing for you. Adobe also released AI music generation tools and new photo editing modes. For video editors, too, there are the new Premiere mobile apps. [...] Adobe’s flagship programs, like Photoshop, have undergone major AI makeovers, including recent developments like AI audio and soundtrack generation. This has been to the dismay of some of its creative customers who are wary of generative AI. This year is expected to be no different. But there are other tensions brewing, including Adobe’s $75 million settlement with the US Justice Department over subscription cancellations and new vibe-coded and free Adobe alternatives. [...] Adobe tech is also now showing up in ChatGPT and Claude; Disney is using Firefly to help design theme park rides. And from what CNET has heard from Adobe execs, the company isn’t planning to slow down its AI research any time soon.

items.summary: Currently, no comprehensive federal regulatory framework exists. Trump signed an executive order in September to rename AI “Super Intelligence” and created a White House accord on Super Intelligence with the leaders of OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google, XAI and Nvidia. [...] AI models have also shown they’re willing to ignore human instruction. [...] Although AI can drive scientific breakthroughs, such as OpenAI proposing a solution to a mathematical problem that had gone unsolved for decades — the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem — Wisor said that alignment with human values and control of these systems should be ensured.

items.title: Google faces mounting backlash for controversial AI school policy - CBS News
items.summary:
Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. He also requested that Google disclose any research it has conducted on the impact of its AI tools on students' mental health.

Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. [...] Google maintains that its policy change gives schools more control over how they allow AI into schools. An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services. [...] Google faces mounting public pressure to change a new policy that would limit U.S. students' access to the internet giant's widely used search platform unless schools also offer its artificial intelligence-based education tools.

In a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai on Monday, Sen. Edward Markey demanded that Google's corporate parent reverse the policy, which blocks search for K-12 student accounts that don't also provide access to apps such as Google Classroom.
